heroIntro: Under Sections 261 to 263 of the Income Tax Act 2023, taxpayers cannot delete an e-TIN online themselves; instead, they must submit a formal written deactivation petition to their assigned Deputy Commissioner of Taxes (DCT). Once three years of returns and tax clearances are verified, future return obligations stop.

sections.title: Legal Grounds to Deactivate or Cancel an e-TIN
sections.content:
Tax registration in Bangladesh remains permanently active until formally cancelled or deactivated by order of the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes under Section 262 of the Income Tax Act 2023. Thousands of citizens who opened an e-TIN for a temporary credit card, student bank deposit, or employment application discover that the NBR e-TIN portal offers no self-service delete option.

Sections 261, 262, and 263 authorize the DCT to deactivate, suspend, or cancel an e-TIN upon verified proof that: the taxpayer has permanently ceased earning taxable income, permanently emigrated abroad without domestic assets, dissolved a registered business, holds a duplicate e-TIN in error, or has passed away. Each petition requires settling prior filing arrears and verifying zero tax demand before administrative closure takes legal effect.

Until written cancellation is granted, you remain legally bound to submit annual zero income tax returns so penalties under Section 174 do not accumulate. Leaving an unused e-TIN unfiled also risks triggering automated tax assessment notices and adverse entries across business VAT compliance records.

sections.title: Procedure to Apply for TIN Cancellation Before the DCT
sections.content:
Canceling an e-TIN is a formal quasi-judicial process initiated in writing at the exact Tax Circle printed at the bottom of your e-TIN certificate under Section 262. Following the structured statutory workflow ensures the DCT processes your closure file without procedural rejection or circle transfer delays:

  1. Clear Outstanding Return Backlog: Before applying, submit any unfiled returns from the preceding three assessment years and pay pending tax dues or applicable delay penalties under Section 174.
  2. Draft a Reasoned Deactivation Petition: Prepare a signed formal application under Section 262 addressed to the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes explaining why taxability has permanently ended.
  3. Submit File with Supporting Proof: File the petition in person or through an authorized tax advocate, obtaining a dated receiving seal and official diary number from the circle desk.
  4. Attend Verification Hearing and Collect Order: Respond to any DCT clarification request, obtain a Tax Clearance Certificate if needed, and retain the official written cancellation order once NBR updates your e-TIN status.

If your file has pending appellate disputes, complete income tax appellate proceedings beforehand so no open tax demand blocks administrative closure.

sections.title: Required Documents Checklist for TIN Deactivation
sections.content:
Tax circle officers strictly scrutinize evidence proving zero ongoing domestic income or business liquidation before approving permanent TIN closure under Sections 261 and 262. Submitting well-organized, legible evidence prevents repeated hearing adjournments. Attach attested photocopies alongside originals for inspection when filing at the Tax Zone desk, and retain your dated receiving copy securely throughout verification:

  • Formal application addressed to the DCT specifying exact Section 262 deactivation grounds, Tax Zone code, and contact particulars.
  • Printed copy of the existing e-TIN certificate and clear National ID or valid passport identification copy.
  • Return acknowledgments or PSR certificates covering the last three consecutive assessment years.
  • Updated bank statements and account closure certificates demonstrating settled financial obligations and absence of active taxable interest.
  • For deceased taxpayers: official City Corporation or Union Parishad death certificate plus legal heir succession documentation under Section 194.
  • For closed firms or companies: RJSC dissolution proof, trade license surrender receipt, and BIN cancellation order.

Emigrants relocating abroad should include permanent residency visas, exit immigration stamps, and notarized proof showing transfer of local income-producing property.

sections.title: Deceased Taxpayers, NRBs, and Closed Companies
sections.content:
Section 194 and Section 262 of the Income Tax Act 2023 govern special TIN deactivation rules for estates of deceased persons, non-residents, and wound-up corporate entities. Legal heirs frequently underestimate how an unclosed deceased e-TIN delays bank FDR release, ancestral land mutation, and civil succession proceedings, while closed businesses keep accruing statutory non-filing penalties until BIN and municipal trade license records are formally closed alongside their tax circle file.

NRBs unable to travel to Dhaka may execute an embassy-attested Power of Attorney authorizing counsel to settle arrears and complete the circle hearing remotely.

sections.title: Conclusion and Legal Support
sections.content:
Formally canceling an unnecessary or deceased person's e-TIN stops recurring Section 174 late penalties permanently and prevents asset-transfer delays for heirs. Never abandon an e-TIN simply because your salary ended or you relocated abroad; without a formal written deactivation order from the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes under Section 262, NBR computer records keep flagging annual non-filing, generating compliance notices, and obstructing PSR-dependent banking or registry transactions.

faqs.question: Can I delete my e-TIN certificate online through the NBR website?
faqs.answer: No. The National Board of Revenue e-TIN portal has no online delete or self-cancellation button. Under Section 262 of the Income Tax Act 2023, you must apply in writing to your assigned Deputy Commissioner of Taxes with return acknowledgments and proof explaining why taxable status has ended.

faqs.question: How many years of tax returns must be filed before canceling a TIN?
faqs.answer: In standard practice, Tax Circles require proof of filed returns—including zero returns where applicable—for at least the last three assessment years alongside confirmation that no tax arrears remain unpaid. Filing pending returns beforehand ensures the DCT accepts your Section 262 closure petition smoothly.

faqs.question: How do legal heirs cancel the TIN certificate of a deceased parent?
faqs.answer: Under Sections 194 and 262 of the Income Tax Act 2023, the executor or legal heir must file a written petition at the deceased taxpayer's circle enclosing the death certificate, succession or warish certificate, and final return up to the date of death so future assessments stop.

faqs.question: How long does TIN cancellation approval take in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Once complete documentation and prior three-year clearances are lodged, verification and issuance of the formal deactivation order by the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes generally takes 30 to 60 working days. Files involving tax audits, transfer between circles, or pending appeals may take slightly longer.

faqs.question: Can a deactivated TIN be reactivated later if I start earning taxable income again?
faqs.answer: Yes. Because e-TIN profiles remain tied permanently to your National ID number in NBR records, if you resume business or cross the taxable threshold in future years, you can petition the Tax Circle under Section 261 to reactivate the existing registration and resume annual e-Return filing.
